correctness.rationale: The graph has 12 distinct balls. Exact linearization yields all 486 centered and 21,875 uncentered matrices. The standalone integer Bareiss/Sylvester certificate strictly bounds respectively 485 and 21,870 matrices; the only remaining matrices are a unique centered winner and five rotated uncentered winners. Explicit positive eigenvectors, cubic root isolation, and strict ball-choice inequalities establish attainment and complete equality cases. The checker was run successfully and its actual embedded source is included. There is no extrapolation from finite samples.

value.rationale: The pentagonal wheel is the first wheel with an odd nontriangular rim, a canonical diameter-two planar hub-and-cycle graph. The exact centered-to-uncentered gap and change from one rotationally invariant extremizer to five symmetry-broken rays demonstrate nontrivial structural dependence on whether averaging centers can move. Both exact values and all equality cases are motivated analytic invariants, not a routine number or arbitrary parameter slice.
